title: $102,030 a Year to Make Cartoons
description:
Making cartoons pays 102,030 dollars a year. That's the median.

Sources:
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Special effects artists and animators 27-1014, annual median wage, May 2025: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000027101413
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Special effects artists and animators, 10th percentile: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000027101411
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Special effects artists and animators, 90th percentile: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000027101415
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Special effects artists and animators, employment: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000027101401

BLS May 2025 (OEWS), special effects artists and animators (27-1014): 19,970 jobs on payrolls (OEWS does not count the self-employed); median $102,030; 10th percentile $58,600; 90th percentile $177,110. Median = half earn more, half earn less. Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Making cartoons pays 102,030 dollars a year. That's the median.
But it's a small club. Just 19,970 jobs on US payrolls.
Starting out? The bottom ten percent earn under 58,600.
But right in the middle? That 102,030 dollars.
Then the top ten percent pass 177,000. For drawing dragons.
